_comment: CanDo reference values extracted from the honeycomb 6HB/210bp battery (2026-07-03). These are the calibration/validation targets for the native NADOC FEM. Bends measured from deformedShape.bild + atomic PDB (arc-span + chord-sagitta, agree <1deg). Twist measured via 6-fold order parameter on coarse axis nodes (|Z|~0.9, linear profile, control=0); absolute sign is arbitrary (PCA frame), magnitude +/-~15pct method uncertainty. RMSF from structure_NMA_RMSF.txt (nm).

07_2hb_twist.note: 2-helix, 5 skips/helix; user added nicks to linearize staples before submit; seamless-routed

10_18hb_bend.caveat: mild non-planarity (bend-twist coupling in larger cross-section); span/sagitta agree ~4deg

cross_section_scaling_finding: At the SAME 5-skips/helix density (analytic 171deg for ALL), CanDo global twist DROPS with bundle size: 2HB=84deg (0.49), 6HB=45deg (0.26), 18HB=23deg (0.14) — roughly halves as helix count triples. The naive analytic is cross-section-blind (171 for all); only a proper FE captures the torsional-coupling size dependence. 2HB anchors GJ (weakest coupling); 6HB/18HB pin the coupling scaling. CAVEAT: 07/09 submitted topology has user-added nicks (staples appeared cyclic in caDNAno though our export traces linear); the global twist trend is robust but exact per-design FEM matching wants the user's submitted files.
key_finding: CanDo reproduces BEND at ~95% of the naive single-helix analytic but TWIST at only ~14-49% (dropping with bundle size). The analytic 34.3deg/deletion ignores the bundle's torsional coupling; crossover-linked helices resist global twist. The native FEM MUST reproduce this bend/twist asymmetry AND the twist-damping-vs-cross-section scaling — the naive analytic cannot. RMSF ~0.4-1.7nm (stiff crossover-dense core -> floppy ends), consistent across designs.
